findings.basis: 37 of these 119 profiles already get true from the Google lane, so nothing changes for them. For the rest the value is a carrier setting that ships on real devices for a SIM that exists. Google's current Pixel CarrierSettings (2026-09/10 translations, 11 to 24 Pixel models) sets true for Yoigo/MASMOVIL, Telekom HR, A1/Vivacom/Yettel BG, the Dish 5G SA ranges on 302-220, T-Mobile 311-660, Cellcom 311-840, FirstNet 313-110/120, Dish 313-340 and the T-Mobile US networks. AOSP's carrier_config_carrierid_1839_Verizon-Wireless.xml:38, which this ROM also ships in its CarrierConfig assets, sets true for Verizon. OEM vendor.xml carrier configs set true per carrier, not as a blanket default: the MediaTek mt6768 set marks 65 of 817 entries, Sony sm8250 14 of 281 and Motorola sm7250 61 of 392. That covers AT&T 310-070/090/680/980 (about 300 device sources, 2019-2024), TELUS, C Spire, Southern Linc, Verizon LRA-partner GID1s, the Sprint-affiliate SPN entries, Boost, Airtel/Jio/Reliance (Sony, 2019-2023) and the 2026 MediaTek set for Orange MD/LU/Caraibe/Reunion, Telekom MK/ME, SPM Telecom and O2 262-11. For several of these (for example airtel_in, rjio_in, orange_md, telekom_mk, cspire_us, TELUS) Google's own entry leaves the key unset rather than setting it false, so the only explicit setting is the OEM one.
findings.effect: rtt_supported_bool (CarrierConfigManager.java:3415-3418, default false at :12190) is read in four places that change call handling. (1) ImsManager.updateRttConfigValue (frameworks/opt/net/ims ImsManager.java:2756-2797): with the key true and ignore_rtt_mode_setting_bool at its default true (CarrierConfigManager.java:11996) it provisions RTT_SETTING_ENABLED=1 into the ImsService and keeps IMS turned on even when nothing else needs it (ImsManager.java:1763-1785); with false it provisions 0. (2) The AOSP ImsStack's ImsRegistrationTracker adds Capability.TEXT next to every VOICE capability when that provisioning item is 1, using rtt_supported_while_roaming_bool when roaming (ImsRegistrationTracker.java:419-424, 585-598), so the normal REGISTER carries the text media feature tag; AosRegistration.UpdateNetworkFeatureRtt marks TEXT unavailable when the network does not confirm it (AosRegistration.cpp:1210-1245). (3) The native stack reads the key directly (CarrierConfig.java:62-90 forwards it; AosNConfiguration.cpp:149-157, 1568-1570): AosHandleEmergencyMtc adds TEXT to the emergency registration whenever the key is true, with no roaming or network check (AosHandleEmergencyMtc.cpp:45-63), and AosCondition.IsDeregRequiredForTty deregisters IMS in TTY mode only when RTT is unsupported, VoLTE TTY is unsupported and the UE is combined-attached (AosCondition.cpp:813-826, 998-1031). (4) Every MO, emergency and conference call type is cut down to the registered features, so an RTT request on a registration without TEXT is placed as plain voice, and an incoming text offer is accepted only with TEXT registered (CallTypeUtil.cpp:24-66, IdleState.cpp:113-117, MtcSession.cpp:86-89, 541-553); a voice call's SDP is audio-only either way (MtcMediaUtil.cpp:306-326). TTY routing is decided by carrier_volte_tty_supported_bool, not by this key (ImsManager.java:1751; EmergencyCallDomainSelector.java:755-756, 1168). Telephony's own RTT gates also need R.bool.config_support_rtt, which is false in this tree (packages/services/Telephony/res/values/config.xml:234-235, config_support_simless_emergency_rtt false at :259-261) with no overlay in device/samsung/x1s, device/samsung/universal9830-common or rom-repos/android_vendor_extra: PhoneInterfaceManager.isRttSupported/isRttEnabled (PhoneInterfaceManager.java:7995-8035), the PhoneAccount CAPABILITY_RTT bit (TelecomAccountRegistry.java:441-446, 1102-1155) and the accessibility RTT switch (AccessibilitySettingsFragment.java:267-276) are all off, so the stock Dialer never offers or upgrades to RTT (DialerCall.java:1024-1052). Telecom still creates RTT streams for an incoming RTT call (CallsManager.java:1809-1816) and for an outgoing emergency call when the calling app passes EXTRA_START_CALL_WITH_RTT, ignoring the account capability (CallsManager.java:2650-2662). Read on the LineageOS 23.2 tree; the phone runs 24.0, whose config_support_rtt was not checked. The OCD ImsStack fork (branch ocd) is byte-identical to the tree in every ImsStack file cited.
findings.risk: Compared with Android's default false: an ordinary 112/911 voice call is routed and offered exactly as before (audio-only SDP, same domain selection); the emergency REGISTER gains the standard text media feature tag, which a network without RTT ignores. Outgoing RTT, emergency included, can only be started by a third-party app passing EXTRA_START_CALL_WITH_RTT. With true the stack then offers text where the emergency registration carries TEXT; with false it quietly places voice. Incoming RTT calls and PSAP RTT callbacks are answered as RTT only where the network confirmed TEXT, and otherwise as voice. TTY calls route the same way because carrier_volte_tty_supported_bool decides that. True only stops the native stack's TTY-mode IMS deregistration, after the framework has already taken VoLTE voice away for TTY. IMS stays on when the user turns VoLTE off, but voice still follows the MMTEL voice capability, so CS routing does not change. No priority (WPS) path reads the key. The remaining exposure is an RTT emergency request from a third-party app on a network whose E-CSCF mishandles a text offer. That is a narrow path that the stock UI cannot reach, and on the carriers above RTT is the intended behaviour.

notes: Proceed. On LineageOS with the AOSP ImsStack, rtt_supported_bool turns on RTT provisioning and the TEXT feature in the normal and emergency registrations. It never changes how a voice emergency call is routed or what media it offers, and it does not change TTY routing. The normal-registration TEXT capability falls back to off on networks that do not confirm it. For these profiles the value is either what the Google lane already serves or a real carrier setting from Google's current Pixel data, AOSP's Verizon config or selective OEM carrier configs for SIMs that exist. Serving it makes RTT calls and callbacks work where the network supports them, without putting a 112/911, TTY or priority call at risk. Correction, 2026-11-06 (rule round 61, item 4): the AOSP CarrierConfig assets this read names are a source, and they are not read on an OCD ROM. OCD's overlay points platform_carrier_config_package at com.android.carriersettings, so the assets are no lower layer and serve nothing there. read_at and findings stay as first written. The basis 'nothing changes' is wrong for every bundle this read acts on: a read of a Google-family value acts only where the SIM's own Google entry says something else. The Dish 5G SA ranges on 302-220 reach no SIM through this read. Current counts are 62 of 628 scopes for MediaTek and 13 of 72 for Sony. 3 of the 12 ImsStack fork files compared differ from the tree, none on an RTT path. Verizon's 27 bundles get this value through this read alone, so any change to that item needs its own served diff. open.312120.5e45524c258b left main and left this read, and sony_open_devices_aosp, which backed no listed profile, left its families. The 28 profiles with no recorded source family moved to hold rtt_supported_bool.1381f3aecbc2: this read served nothing there. Rule round 61 moved 61 profiles to holds: rtt_supported_bool.5f8e0803b132 (37, one maker), rtt_supported_bool.af4be128cd2a (2, against Google's false) and rtt_supported_bool.da4a3f78a281 (22, another entry's value). 29 active profiles stay here.
